t: Socrates wrote no texts and is known mainly through his pupils Plato and Xenophon, the comic dramatist Aristophanes and Aristotle, whose often contradictory accounts make up what is called the Socratic problem.

He questioned Athenians who were thought to be experts, showed that their definitions of virtues such as courage and justice contradicted themselves, and said that he was sure only that he did not know.

In 399 BCE a jury of hundreds of male citizens found him guilty of impiety and of corrupting the youth, and he drank hemlock after refusing his friends' offer to help him escape; scholars still disagree about why he was convicted.
dyk: Of all the works written about Socrates' trial, only three survive: Plato's Apology, Xenophon's Apology and Xenophon's Memorabilia.
ev: Born in the Athenian deme of Alopece to Sophroniscus and Phaenarete, in 470 or 469 BCE
The Thirty Tyrants begin to rule Athens; under them Socrates and four others are told to arrest Leon the Salaminian, and Socrates alone refuses, according to Plato's Apology
An amnesty is granted to Athenian citizens to prevent civil war after the fall of the Thirty

Accused by Meletus, Anytus and Lycon of impiety and corrupting the youth, he is tried before a jury of hundreds of citizens, sentenced to death, and drinks hemlock after refusing an escape offered by his friends
Friedrich Schleiermacher's essay on the worth of Socrates as a philosopher attacks Xenophon's accounts, and the attack is widely accepted
Nietzsche's The Birth of Tragedy holds Socrates responsible for the deterioration of ancient Greek civilisation

f.born: 470 or 469 BCE in the Athenian deme of Alopece, an Athenian citizen; son of Sophroniscus, a stoneworker, and Phaenarete, a midwife
f.died: 399 BCE in Athens, by drinking hemlock after being sentenced to death for impiety and corrupting the young; according to the Phaedo, his last words concerned a rooster owed to Asclepius
f.role: Athenian philosopher; soldier in three campaigns of the Peloponnesian War, according to Plato; held no office and never ran for one
f.known: the Socratic method of questioning (elenchus); his claim of ignorance; the search for definitions of the virtues; the view that virtue is knowledge; his trial and death; his influence on Plato and on later schools
